events.title: Jules Verne is born in Nantes
events.summary: The author of Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea is born.
events.description: On February 8, 1828, the French writer Jules Verne was born in Nantes. His Extraordinary Journeys included Journey to the Centre of the Earth and Around the World in Eighty Days.
events.notificationTitle: The writer who imagined the future
events.notificationBody: In 1828, Jules Verne, author of Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea, was born in Nantes.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Jules Verne

events.title: Skylab 4 returns after a record 84 days in space
events.summary: The crew of the last Skylab mission splashes down in the Pacific.
events.description: On February 8, 1974, the Skylab 4 crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean after 84 days in space, a new record for space endurance.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 8

events.title: Mary, Queen of Scots, is beheaded
events.summary: Elizabeth I's rival is executed at Fotheringhay Castle.
events.description: On February 8, 1587, Mary, Queen of Scots, the rival of Queen Elizabeth I of England, was beheaded at Fotheringhay Castle.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 8

events.title: The Dawes General Allotment Act becomes law
events.summary: The US law breaks up Native American reservation land into allotments.
events.description: On February 8, 1887, the United States passed the Dawes General Allotment Act, providing for the distribution of Native American reservation land.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 8

events.title: James Dean is born
events.summary: The actor who came to symbolize restless youth is born.
events.description: On February 8, 1931, the American actor James Dean was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 8

events.title: Element 112 is created in Germany
events.summary: Physicists make the heavy element later named copernicium.
events.description: On February 9, 1996, the German physicist Peter Armbruster and his team synthesized chemical element 112, a heavy element later named copernicium in honor of the astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus.
events.notificationTitle: A new element joins the table
events.notificationBody: In 1996, scientists in Germany made element 112, later named copernicium after Copernicus.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 9
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Copernicium

events.title: The Treaty of Alinagar puts Calcutta under British control
events.summary: The agreement is a prelude to the British seizure of Bengal.
events.description: On February 9, 1757, the Treaty of Alinagar placed what is today Kolkata under British control, a prelude to the British seizure of Bengal.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 9

events.title: J.M. Coetzee is born
events.summary: The South African novelist and future Nobel laureate is born.
events.description: On February 9, 1940, the South African novelist, critic and translator J.M. Coetzee was born. He won the 2003 Nobel Prize for Literature.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 9

events.title: Alice Walker is born
events.summary: The author of The Color Purple is born.
events.description: On February 9, 1944, the American writer Alice Walker was born. She is perhaps best known for her Pulitzer Prize-winning novel The Color Purple (1982).

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 9

events.title: Soviet leader Yury Andropov dies
events.summary: He is replaced by Konstantin Chernenko after 15 months in power.
events.description: On February 9, 1984, the Soviet leader Yury Andropov died, 15 months after succeeding Leonid Brezhnev. He was replaced by Konstantin Chernenko.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 9

events.title: U-2 pilot Francis Gary Powers is exchanged for a Soviet spy
events.summary: The Cold War foes swap Powers for Rudolf Abel.
events.description: On February 10, 1962, Francis Gary Powers, the American U-2 pilot shot down over the Soviet Union in 1960, was exchanged for the jailed Soviet spy Rudolf Abel.
events.notificationBody: In 1962, U-2 pilot Francis Gary Powers was traded for the Soviet spy Rudolf Abel.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 10
Encyclopaedia Britannica - U-2 Incident

events.title: The Treaty of Paris ends the Seven Years' War
events.summary: France and Britain settle the conflicts behind the war.
events.description: On February 10, 1763, the Treaty of Paris was signed, ending the territorial conflicts between France and Britain that had caused the Seven Years' War.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 10

events.title: Queen Victoria marries Prince Albert
events.summary: The young queen weds her German cousin.
events.description: On February 10, 1840, Queen Victoria of Great Britain married Prince Albert.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 10

events.title: Bertolt Brecht is born in Augsburg
events.summary: The German poet and playwright is born.
events.description: On February 10, 1898, the poet and playwright Bertolt Brecht was born in Augsburg, Germany.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 10

events.title: Mark Spitz is born
events.summary: The swimmer who will win seven gold medals at one Olympics is born.
events.description: On February 10, 1950, the American swimmer Mark Spitz was born. He became the first athlete to win seven gold medals at a single Olympic Games.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 10

events.title: Nelson Mandela is released from prison
events.summary: He walks free after 27 years and begins talks to end apartheid.
events.description: On February 11, 1990, Nelson Mandela was released after 27 years in prison. He went on to negotiate with President F.W. de Klerk the end of apartheid in South Africa.
events.notificationBody: In 1990, Nelson Mandela walked out of prison after 27 years.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 11

events.title: The Lateran Treaty creates Vatican City
events.summary: Italy recognizes papal sovereignty over an enclave in Rome.
events.description: On February 11, 1929, Benito Mussolini of Italy and Pietro Gasparri of the Vatican signed the Lateran Treaty, recognizing papal sovereignty over Vatican City, an enclave in Rome.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 11

events.title: Hosni Mubarak steps down in Egypt
events.summary: Pro-democracy protests end nearly 30 years of rule.
events.description: On February 11, 2011, Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak stepped down after nearly 30 years in power, following the pro-democracy uprisings known as the Arab Spring.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 11

events.title: Thomas Edison is born in Ohio
events.summary: The inventor of the phonograph is born.
events.description: On February 11, 1847, the inventor Thomas Edison was born in Ohio.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 11

events.title: Margaret Thatcher becomes leader of Britain's Conservative Party
events.summary: She replaces Edward Heath at the head of the party.
events.description: On February 11, 1975, Margaret Thatcher was elected leader of Britain's Conservative Party, replacing Edward Heath.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 11

events.title: Charles Darwin is born
events.summary: The naturalist behind the theory of evolution by natural selection is born.
events.description: On February 12, 1809, Charles Darwin, who developed the theory of evolution by natural selection, was born in England. Abraham Lincoln was born on the same day.
events.notificationTitle: Born the same day as Lincoln
events.notificationBody: In 1809, Charles Darwin was born in England, on the very same day as Abraham Lincoln.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 12

events.title: Abraham Lincoln is born
events.summary: The 16th US president, who preserved the Union, is born.
events.description: On February 12, 1809, Abraham Lincoln was born. As the 16th president of the United States (1861-65), he preserved the Union during the American Civil War.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 12

events.title: Puyi, China's last emperor, abdicates
events.summary: The abdication ends imperial rule in China.
events.description: On February 12, 1912, Puyi, the last emperor of China, abdicated at the end of the Chinese Revolution.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 12

events.title: Chile formally declares independence
events.summary: The declaration comes a year after San Martin's revolutionary forces won a key victory.
events.description: On February 12, 1818, Chile formally declared its independence, exactly one year after revolutionary forces led by Jose de San Martin won a victory.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 12

events.title: Thieves steal The Scream from Oslo's National Gallery
events.summary: Edvard Munch's painting is taken in a break-in.
events.description: On February 12, 1994, thieves broke into the National Gallery in Oslo and stole a version of Edvard Munch's The Scream. The painting was recovered several months later.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 12
Encyclopaedia Britannica - The Scream

events.title: The last Peanuts comic strip is published
events.summary: It appears hours after the death of creator Charles Schulz.
events.description: On February 13, 2000, the last Peanuts comic strip was published, just hours after the death of its creator, Charles Schulz.
events.notificationBody: In 2000, the last Peanuts strip ran, just hours after its creator, Charles Schulz, died.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 13

events.title: Australia's prime minister apologizes to Aboriginal peoples
events.summary: Kevin Rudd apologizes for abuses under earlier governments.
events.description: On February 13, 2008, Australian Prime Minister Kevin Rudd apologized to Australia's Aboriginal peoples for abuses they had suffered under earlier administrations.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 13

events.title: France tests its first atomic bomb in the Sahara
events.summary: France becomes a nuclear power.
events.description: On February 13, 1960, France detonated its first atomic bomb, in the Sahara desert.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 13

events.title: Richard Wagner dies in Venice
events.summary: The German composer dies at 69.
events.description: On February 13, 1883, the German composer Richard Wagner died in Venice at age 69.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 13

events.title: Georges Simenon is born in Liege
events.summary: The creator of Inspector Maigret is born.
events.description: On February 13, 1903, the Belgian-French novelist Georges Simenon, creator of the Parisian police inspector Jules Maigret, was born in Liege, Belgium.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 13
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Georges Simenon

events.title: The ENIAC computer is announced to the public
events.summary: A 30-ton machine is unveiled as the first general-purpose electronic computer.
events.description: On February 14, 1946, the ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer), the first general-purpose electronic computer, was announced to the public. Built at the University of Pennsylvania, it used about 18,000 vacuum tubes and weighed 30 tons.
events.notificationBody: In 1946, the ENIAC, a 30-ton machine with 18,000 vacuum tubes, was announced to the world.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 14
Penn Engineering - ENIAC

events.title: Captain James Cook is killed in Hawaii
events.summary: The British explorer dies at Kealakekua Bay.
events.description: On February 14, 1779, the British explorer Captain James Cook was killed by Hawaiians at Kealakekua Bay.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 14

events.title: Arizona becomes the 48th US state
events.summary: It is the last of the contiguous states to join the Union.
events.description: On February 14, 1912, Arizona became a US state, the last of the 48 contiguous states to be admitted to the Union.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Arizona

events.title: YouTube is registered
events.summary: Three founders register a website for sharing videos.
events.description: On February 14, 2005, Steve Chen, Chad Hurley and Jawed Karim registered YouTube, a website for sharing videos.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 14

events.title: South African President Jacob Zuma resigns
events.summary: He steps down amid scandals and corruption allegations.
events.description: On February 14, 2018, South African President Jacob Zuma resigned amid scandals and corruption allegations.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 14
